description: G11 regression canary (Trial-2): two articles from different sources share the same base headline but with MULTI-WORD attribution suffixes. After normalizeHeadline strips the suffix, both become identical, and url-absent dedup key is identical → articleCount must be 1. A naive fix that only strips single-word attributions (/ - \w+$/) fails to strip 'The Financial Times' or 'Nikkei Asia Review', leaving the two normalized headlines different → dedup key diverges → articleCount becomes 2, FAILING this scenario.

articles.headline: Vietnam GDP rises 6.8% in Q1 2026 - The Financial Times
Vietnam GDP rises 6.8% in Q1 2026 - Nikkei Asia Review

note: Both articles normalize to 'Vietnam GDP rises 6.8% in Q1 2026'. Same source='reuters', url=null → dedup key = 'headline:reuters:vietnam gdp rises 6.8% in q1 2026' → first-wins dedup removes second. articleCount=1 ONLY if normalization correctly strips MULTI-WORD attributions like ' - The Financial Times' and ' - Nikkei Asia Review'. A naive single-word-only fix misses these, producing different normalized strings → articleCount=2.
